Senses.Note: Family comparison: 'who?' (誰) and 'which one?' (阿那箇) are interrogatives; 'that one' (那箇) and 'this one' (這箇) are demonstratives; 'who?' (阿誰) does not acquire a separate 'true self' sense merely because identity is sometimes its subject. Agent, author, beneficiary, and lineage predecessor are different answers to the same pronoun, not different referents encoded by the word. Senses.Explanation: An interrogative pronoun: 'who?' or, according to syntax, 'whom?' The records put it to several public uses. It asks the recorded questioner's identity inside the exchange 'what is buddha?' — 'who are you?' / 'so-and-so' / 'do you recognize so-and-so?' (汝是阿誰／某甲／汝識某甲否). It asks lineage in the stock interview formula 'whose song does the identified master sing; to whom does the house style succeed?' (師唱誰家曲，宗風嗣阿誰), agency in 'who can go?' (阿誰去得), authorship in 'who spoke this scripture?' (此經是阿誰說), and the beneficiary of activity in 'for whom are you busy every day?' (每日區區為阿誰). The Chan deviation lies in this concentration inside public identity, lineage, authorship, and accountability questions; the word itself remains the ordinary interrogative and does not name a special inward self.
